transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, Mr. Potter! Good to see you again. What can I do for you today? Looking for a new broom polish, or perhaps a servicing kit for the Firebolt?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: No, actually, I was just here to return the broom-servicing kit I bought. There's a problem with it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Oh dear, that's not good. Let me have a look at it. Did you bring the kit with you?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, I did. Here it is. As you can see, the handle polish is completely dried out, and the tail-twig clippers are rusted. It's not fit for use.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Hmm, yes, I can see the seal's been broken. I'm afraid all servicing kits are non-refundable once the seal is broken, Mr. Potter. You'll have to take it up with the manufacturer directly — that's a six-week owl exchange minimum.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I see. Well, I hope the manufacturer is as efficient as you are with their customer service, Mr.---?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: It's Perkins, Mr. Potter. And I assure you, Quality Quidditch Supplies prides itself on service. It's just the manufacturer's policy we have to follow.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand, Mr. Perkins. It's just a bit of an inconvenience. I guess I'll have to wait it out, then. Is there anything else you can offer in the meantime to tide me over?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Well, we do have a small selection of individual tools and polishes sold separately. I could offer you a discount on a replacement jar of handle polish and a new set of clippers. It won't be as cheap as the kit, but it'll get your Firebolt back in the air while you wait for the manufacturer.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: That's actually a fair offer, Mr. Perkins. I'll take it. Thanks for the help. I'll be back if I have any more issues with my broom, though I hope it won't come to that.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Excellent choice, Mr. Potter. I'll ring those up for you now. And of course, we're always here if you need anything else. Safe flying!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Appreciate it, Mr. Perkins. I'll be in the air in no time. Thanks for your assistance. Safe day to you, too!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: My pleasure, Mr. Potter. Do come again.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You can count on it, Mr. Perkins. Til next time, then!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Until next time, Mr. Potter. Take care!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You too, Mr. Perkins! Off to catch the last part of the match before it's all over. I'll be on the pitch next time, though!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I'll be cheering for you, Mr. Potter! Good luck out there!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you! I could use all the support I can get. Particularly against Madame Rochelle's team!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Oh, I've seen her team fly. They're tough, but you've got the Firebolt and the talent. You'll do just fine. Now off you go, before you miss the Snitch!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Right, I'd better not keep her waiting. Thanks again, Mr. Perkins. See you next time!

Openness.behavioral_evidence: He accepts the shopkeeper's alternative solution, showing practical adaptability.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He returns a defective product promptly and explains the specific issues clearly.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: He engages in friendly, extended conversation and mentions going to a match and playing on a team.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He remains polite and cooperative despite inconvenience, thanking the shopkeeper multiple times.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: He handles the product issue calmly without showing frustration or anxiety.
